facts.statement: Calyptosuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaur that lived during the Late Triassic in North America.
facts.quote: Calyptosuchus (meaning "covered crocodile") is an extinct genus of aetosaur from the Late Triassic of North America.

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus was heavily armored and possessed a pig-like snout adapted for uprooting plants.
facts.quote: Like other aetosaurs, it was heavily armored and had a pig-like snout used to uproot plants.

facts.statement: Each row of Calyptosuchus's osteoderms corresponded to one vertebra and consisted of four dorsal osteoderms.
facts.quote: Each row of the osteoderms corresponded to one vertebra, and comprised four dorsal osteoderms.

facts.statement: The rows of osteoderms included two small squarish plates about 10 by 10 cm on the outside and two broader plates approximately 20 by 10 cm on the inside covering most of the back.
facts.quote: Two small squarish osteoderms formed the outside of the row (about 10 by 10 cm), and two much broader osteoderms (approximately 20 by 10 cm) formed the inside of the row and covered most of the back.

facts.statement: The arrangement of its osteoderms likely gave Calyptosuchus a boxy appearance.
facts.quote: This would probably have given it quite a boxy look.

facts.statement: The only skull fragment certainly assigned to Calyptosuchus is a dentary bone, as no other cranial bones have been definitively linked to it.
facts.quote: The only skull fragment that is certainly Calyptosuchus is a dentary bone - no other cranial bones have been assigned to it with certainty.

facts.statement: The preserved dentary bone includes a middle section with an edentulous patch at the front and nine dental alveoli at the rear.
facts.quote: Only a middle part of the dentary is present, with an edentulous patch to the anterior and nine dental alveoli posteriorly.

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus had two very robust sacral vertebrae that were not fused, unlike those of desmatosuchians.
facts.quote: The sacral vertebrae are very robust, and not fused unlike those of desmatosuchians. There are only two sacral vertebrae.

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus possessed at least seventeen caudal vertebrae featuring very tall neural spines and low-attached ribs.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae number at least seventeen, with very tall neural spines (taller than the centrum is) and low-attached caudal ribs.

facts.statement: While earlier publications treated Calyptosuchus as a synonym of Stagonolepis, recent research has determined it is a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Although publications in the 1990s and early 2000s treated the genus as a junior synonym of Stagonolepis, recent work has found it generically distinct from Stagonolepis proper.

facts.statement: The genus Calyptosuchus was established by Long and Ballew in 1985.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Long & Ballew, 1985

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
facts.quote: familia: Stagonolepididae

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus is classified within the subfamily Stagonolepidinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Stagonolepidinae

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus lived during the Late Triassic period in North America.
facts.quote: Calyptosuchus (meaning "covered crocodile") is an extinct genus of aetosaur from the Late Triassic of North America.

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus was heavily armored and used its pig-like snout to uproot plants.
facts.quote: Like other aetosaurs, it was heavily armored and had a pig-like snout used to uproot plants.

facts.statement: Unlike some other armored reptiles, the osteoderms of Calyptosuchus were not entirely fused.
facts.quote: The osteoderms were not entirely fused.

facts.statement: The genus Calyptosuchus was named by Long and Ballew in 1985 based on a partial shell with a spine and pelvis discovered in 1931 by Ermin Cowles Case in the Tecovas Formation of west Texas.
facts.quote: Calyptosuchus fue nombrado por Long y Ballew (1985) sobre la base de UMMP 13950, un caparazón parcial con columna vertebral y pelvis que había sido descubierto en la Formación Tecovas del oeste de Texas en 1931 por Ermin Cowles Case

facts.statement: In a 1932 article, the discoverer Ermin Cowles Case initially assigned the specimen to the group Phytosauria.
facts.quote: quien solo llegó hasta asignar el espécimen a Phytosauria en un artículo de 1932

facts.statement: While publications from the 1990s and early 2000s treated the genus as a synonym of Stagonolepis, recent work has found it to be a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Aunque las publicaciones de la década de 1990 y principios de la de 2000 trataron al género como un sinónimo más moderno de Stagonolepis, trabajos recientes lo han encontrado genéricamente distinto de Stagonolepis

facts.statement: The distinction from Stagonolepis is supported by the discovery of additional material of the same species, including a dentary bone, a possible maxilla, and other neck and trunk vertebrae.
facts.quote: Esto se debe a que se ha descubierto más material de la misma especie, incluido un hueso dentario, un posible maxilar y otras vértebras del cuello y el tronco

facts.statement: Additional fossils found include a femur, a tibia, and extra osteoderms.
facts.quote: También se han encontrado un fémur, tibia y osteodermos adicionales

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus belongs to the parent group Desmatosuchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Desmatosuchinae

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
facts.quote: Family: Stagonolepididae

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Calyptosuchus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 45 recorded fossil occurrences of Calyptosuchus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 45
